㊭ I think we sohuld get back to the idea of thinking about 小象 as a "prior" for 象, and use the corrections of the provisional reading from 象 as a way to train 小象.  We could include a little bit of material about this training process in the writeup at https://hyperreal.enterprises/xiaoxiang.html

㊯ I'd also like you to give me a short draft paragraph that I can send to Brendan Fong that explains how we are working on using his work.  I'm hoping I might be able to arrange a meeting with him to discuss later this week.  (I know we are in a preliminary phase of this work; but maybe it could lead to a joint publication or something later on.)

reply_text:
㊥ (three answers) Agreed on futon1b: the quote stays there, and handling it is for whoever processes the evidence later, including 象's catch-up. On 小象 as 象's prior, I found the correction signal is currently being thrown away. I recomputed it from your store, and the numbers are below, along with a draft section for the 小象 page. The paragraph for Brendan Fong is at the end.

㊩ (the training signal is lost) The JVM was built to stamp every published fragment with how 象 treated 小象's draft: confirmed it, relabelled it, resegmented it, or had no draft there. But 象 publishes through `session_turn_analysis.py complete`, which never calls that code. So of the 41 analysed turns that had a draft, none records the comparison. The draft and reading files sit side by side, so I recomputed it.

㊢ (what 象 did with 小象's drafts, 41 turns, 156 fragments)

| What happened | Fragments |
|---|---|
| 小象 sure, 象 agreed | 20 |
| 小象 sure, 象 relabelled | 17 |
| 小象 unsure, its top guess right | 39 |
| 小象 unsure, its top guess wrong | 66 |
| 象 cut the sentence differently | 14 |

So 小象's sure labels hold 54% of the time, and its top guess when unsure is right 37% of the time. The commonest relabelling is report-problem → explain (6 times): 小象 hears complaints where 象 hears explanations.

㊭ (training 小象 on the corrections) Three steps:
1. Record the comparison at publish time, in the Python tool or in the JVM when it sees the reading land.
2. When 小象 is rebuilt, use 象's relabels and resegmentations as the training signal. Keep confirmed drafts out, or count them less, so 小象 doesn't learn its own guesses back from 象's agreement. The module already intends this ("a reading confirmed from a draft can be kept out of 小象's training"), but nothing feeds it.
3. Report the five numbers above per edition, so the page can show the prior getting better.

The first two are a small packet. Here's a draft section for xiaoxiang.html:

> **How 小象 learns from 象.** 小象 reads a turn first, in a tenth of a second, and its parse appears at once, marked provisional. 象, a language model, then reads the same turn with 小象's draft in hand and confirms or corrects it, fragment by fragment. 小象 is the prior; 象's reading is the evidence. Each correction is a labelled example of where the prior was wrong, and those, not the readings that merely agree, are what 小象 is retrained on. On the first 41 turns read this way, 象 kept 20 of 小象's 37 confident labels and changed 17; of the 105 fragments 小象 left unsure, its first guess was right in 39. The most frequent correction is a fragment 小象 took for a report of a problem that 象 read as an explanation.

Shall I put it on the staging preview (`site-draft`) for you to look at before it goes live?

㊯ (draft paragraph for Brendan Fong)

> Dear Brendan — I'm working on a multi-agent software environment in which human and AI agents hand work to each other, and I've started using two of your ideas to give it a logic. Following your causal theories paper, each design pattern in our library (an IF/HOWEVER/THEN/BECAUSE argument) is written as a small causal theory, kept separate from its mechanisms. Following your decorated cospans, each theory is made open along an interface. The theories that bear on an incident are glued along shared variables, and we compute counterfactuals on the composite, for example whether a guard pattern already in force would have prevented a particular failure. We are now trying to run this live, after every turn of a conversation: the open ports that remain after gluing are the obligations still outstanding, such as a request nobody has answered, and they drive reminders to the agents involved. It's early, and so far finite and Boolean: the Markov-categorical version, with promises treated as combs, is where we'd like to go and where we'd most value your view. Would you have time for a call later this week? If it turns out to be of interest, I'd be glad to explore writing something up together.

🈳 (check before sending) "IF/HOWEVER/THEN/BECAUSE" and "combs" are our terms. The second rests on the comb paper M-diagramprover cites (arXiv 2404.02017), which I haven't verified is his. Adjust as you like.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(what I checked)
- **The loaded code, end to end.** I recorded a quoted turn through it, using a temporary store rather than yours. The record file doesn't contain the quote text; the quote is only in a new sidecar, `RECORD.quotes.json`, which no brief names.
- **Tests.** A new test checks that neither the record file nor the 象 brief contains the quote or the sidecar's name. The same check covers the Emacs recorder (codex-10 uses the JVM recorder, but the Emacs one had the same leak). The Emacs test fails against the previous version and passes now.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(each reader of your turn)
- **codex-10:** gets your turn exactly as typed.
- **小象's draft:** runs over the text with `QUOTE` in place of the block.
- **象:** reads the record, which has `QUOTE`. Fixed as above.
- **大象 and the HUD:** they read 象's reading and agent replies, not your quote.
- **feed.html:** shows the block in its quoted style (shaded background, left rule, fixed-width font). The feed builder now takes the text from the sidecar.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (one thing outside this) Agent-chat's ordinary evidence row for your turn, the transcript entry written when you send, still stores what you typed, quote included, in futon1b. Nothing annotates that row, but it's there. If you'd rather the quote stayed out of futon1b too, that's a change in `agent-chat.el` I can make. You don't need to wait for it.
